outputs.L1: Provided are a compact inkjet head and an inkjet recording apparatus capable of achieving high resolution and stably ejecting liquid droplets at high frequency while incorporating a structure that enables ink circulation. The inkjet head includes: a plurality of nozzles configured to eject ink; a plurality of pressure chambers that respectively communicate with the plurality of nozzles and are filled with ink; a plurality of pressure-generating portions configured to apply pressure to the ink within the plurality of pressure chambers; a circulation flow passage that branches from an ink flow passage extending from inlets of the pressure chambers to outlets of the nozzles and is configured to discharge the ink from the plurality of pressure chambers; and first and second dampers disposed so as to face the circulation flow passage, each damper being capable of changing the volume of the circulation flow passage through elastic deformation in response to pressure.
outputs.L2: Disclosed are a compact inkjet head and an inkjet recording device that support high-resolution printing and stable, high-frequency droplet ejection while allowing ink circulation. The inkjet head comprises multiple nozzles for discharging ink; multiple ink-filled pressure chambers, each communicating with a corresponding nozzle; multiple pressure-generating units that pressurize the ink within the respective pressure chambers; and a circulation channel branching from an ink path extending between the pressure-chamber inlets and the nozzle outlets, through which ink can be removed from the pressure chambers. First and second dampers face the circulation channel and elastically deform in response to pressure, thereby varying the channel’s volume.
outputs.L3:
The inkjet head and recording apparatus are designed with a compact structure while enabling high-resolution printing. The system supports ink circulation and can stably eject ink droplets at high frequencies, thereby maintaining reliable print quality during high-speed operation.

The inkjet head includes multiple nozzles, each of which communicates with a corresponding pressure chamber filled with ink. Pressure-generating portions apply pressure to the ink in the respective chambers, causing droplets to be discharged through the nozzles.

To facilitate circulation, a branched flow passage directs ink away from the pressure chambers. Two elastic dampers are provided along this circulation passage. These dampers deform in response to pressure fluctuations, adjusting the volume of the passage and suppressing variations in ink pressure. This configuration promotes stable ink circulation and consistent droplet ejection while preserving the compact dimensions of the inkjet head.
outputs.L4:
A compact, high-resolution inkjet head includes a plurality of nozzles arranged at a high density, a plurality of pressure chambers respectively communicating with the nozzles, and pressure generators that selectively change the pressure within the corresponding pressure chambers. When a pressure generator is actuated, a pressure fluctuation is produced in the associated pressure chamber, causing an ink droplet to be ejected through the corresponding nozzle.

The inkjet head further includes an ink-circulation passage through which ink is continuously or intermittently circulated. The circulation passage supplies ink to the pressure chambers and removes ink that has not been ejected. Maintaining such circulation helps prevent sedimentation, local increases in ink viscosity, temperature irregularities, and the accumulation of air bubbles or foreign matter near the nozzles. The circulation passage is branched so that ink can be distributed efficiently among the densely arranged pressure chambers without substantially increasing the size of the head.

Two elastically deformable dampers are provided in communication with the branched circulation passage. Each damper includes a flexible portion that deforms in response to changes in ink pressure, thereby temporarily increasing or decreasing the effective volume of the circulation passage. The dampers absorb pressure waves generated by actuation of the pressure generators and reduce pressure interference between adjacent pressure chambers. Using two dampers at different portions of the branched passage provides balanced pressure control and suppresses both upstream and downstream pressure fluctuations.

During high-frequency operation, repeated actuation of the pressure generators can create rapid pressure variations in the ink flow path. Without adequate damping, these variations may alter droplet volume or velocity, cause unintended droplet ejection, or interfere with ink refill after each ejection. The dual-damper arrangement accommodates the pressure changes by elastically varying the internal volume of the circulation passage. This allows each pressure chamber to refill reliably while the ink continues to circulate.

The dampers and branched flow passage can be integrated into the layered structure of the inkjet head, reducing the need for large external damping chambers or complicated tubing. As a result, the head can remain compact even when it includes a large number of closely spaced nozzles. The arrangement is therefore suitable for high-resolution printing systems that require rapid, uniform, and stable droplet formation.

A recording apparatus incorporating the inkjet head may include an ink supply unit, a circulation pump, a pressure-regulating mechanism, a controller, and a transport mechanism for moving a recording medium relative to the head. The controller drives the pressure generators according to image data while controlling ink circulation through the head. By combining continuous ink circulation with pressure-responsive volume adjustment by the two dampers, the apparatus can maintain a stable internal pressure and consistently eject droplets at high frequency.

Accordingly, the inkjet head and recording apparatus provide improved ejection stability, reduced pressure crosstalk, reliable chamber refilling, and more uniform droplet characteristics. These benefits are achieved while preserving a compact head configuration and supporting high nozzle density, making the design well suited to high-speed, high-resolution recording.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a compact, high-resolution inkjet head with stable high-frequency droplet ejection, ink circulation, pressure chambers, pressure generators, and two elastic dampers facing a circulation flow passage.
counterfactuals.output: An inkjet head includes a plurality of nozzles, pressure chambers respectively communicating with the nozzles, and pressure generators configured to vary pressure within the pressure chambers to eject ink droplets. A circulation flow passage supplies ink to the pressure chambers and returns unejected ink for recirculation. First and second elastic dampers each face the circulation flow passage and elastically deform in response to pressure fluctuations in circulating ink. The dampers suppress pressure waves generated by high-frequency operation of the pressure generators, thereby reducing interference between adjacent pressure chambers and stabilizing droplet volume, velocity, and ejection direction. Arrangement of the two dampers along the circulation flow passage provides effective pressure attenuation within a limited installation area. The inkjet head therefore supports a compact, high-density nozzle configuration while maintaining stable high-frequency droplet ejection and reliable ink circulation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an inkjet recording apparatus invention that circulates ink through branched flow passages and uses first and second deformable dampers to regulate pressure and passage volume.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is an inkjet recording apparatus in which ink is continuously circulated between an ink tank and a recording head. The circulation path includes a main flow passage that branches into multiple passages connected to nozzle groups or pressure chambers in the recording head, helping distribute fresh ink uniformly and remove bubbles or sediment.

A first damper and a second damper are provided at different portions of the branched flow passages. Each damper includes a flexible or deformable wall that moves in response to ink-pressure changes. Deformation of the first damper suppresses pressure pulsations produced by a pump or by ink ejection and stabilizes the pressure supplied to the branches. The second damper deforms to increase or decrease the effective volume of another passage section, compensating for transient flow differences among the branches and pressure variations on the return side.

By coordinating the pressure-absorbing action of the two dampers, the apparatus maintains suitable nozzle pressure while permitting reliable ink circulation. This reduces meniscus disturbance, ink leakage, nozzle starvation, bubble retention, and uneven discharge, thereby improving recording stability and image quality.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal patent-style summary beginning with “Provided are an inkjet head and an inkjet recording apparatus,” emphasizing compactness, high resolution, and stable high-frequency ink ejection.
counterfactuals.output: Provided are an inkjet head and an inkjet recording apparatus, capable of achieving a compact configuration, high-resolution recording, and stable high-frequency ink ejection. The inkjet head includes a plurality of nozzles arranged at high density, pressure chambers communicating with the respective nozzles, actuators configured to apply pressure to ink in the pressure chambers, and a flow-path structure configured to supply and discharge ink efficiently. The arrangement of the nozzles, pressure chambers, actuators, and associated drive circuitry reduces the overall head size while suppressing thermal and fluidic interference between adjacent ejection channels. Improved ink circulation and pressure control reduce air-bubble retention and pressure fluctuations, thereby maintaining uniform droplet volume and ejection direction even during high-frequency operation. The inkjet recording apparatus includes the inkjet head and a controller configured to control the actuators in accordance with image data, enabling compact, high-speed, and high-definition recording with enhanced ejection stability and reliability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the key components and benefits of an inkjet head containing multiple nozzles, corresponding pressure chambers, pressure-generating portions, a circulation flow passage, and two pressure-responsive dampers.
counterfactuals.output:
### Key components
- **Multiple nozzles** that eject ink droplets.
- **Individual pressure chambers**, each communicating with a corresponding nozzle.
- **Pressure-generating portions**—such as piezoelectric actuators—that vary chamber pressure to discharge ink.
- **A circulation flow passage** that continuously routes ink through or around the pressure chambers, supporting ink supply and return.
- **Two pressure-responsive dampers** that deform in response to pressure fluctuations within the circulation passage.

### Main benefits
- The two dampers absorb pressure waves and reduce hydraulic interference between nozzles.
- More stable chamber and meniscus pressure improves droplet volume, velocity, and placement consistency.
- Ink circulation helps remove bubbles, prevent sedimentation or drying, and reduce nozzle clogging.
- Improved pressure control supports reliable, high-speed, high-density printing across many nozzles.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an English patent abstract for a printhead architecture in which ink can be discharged from pressure chambers through a circulation passage whose volume is varied by elastically deformable dampers.
counterfactuals.output: A printhead includes a plurality of pressure chambers configured to contain ink, nozzles communicating with the respective pressure chambers, and actuators configured to vary the volumes of the pressure chambers to eject ink through the nozzles. A circulation passage communicates with the pressure chambers and permits ink to be discharged from the pressure chambers and circulated through the printhead. At least a portion of a wall defining the circulation passage is formed by one or more elastically deformable dampers. Deformation of the dampers varies a volume of the circulation passage to generate or assist ink flow, absorb pressure fluctuations, and regulate pressure within the pressure chambers. The dampers may be passively deformable in response to ink pressure or actively driven by corresponding drive elements. The architecture promotes removal of bubbles and stagnant ink, stabilizes meniscus pressure, and improves discharge consistency while reducing the size and complexity of an external circulation system.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
